environment: Windows 11 Pro x64, MSVC 14.51; reviewer: an independent agent given only the code, not our conclusions
game_exe_sha256: N/A (prototype does not touch the game)
objective: Independent code review of the networking prototype, as required by the project's collaboration rules.
hypothesis: A reviewer without our context finds defects that the tests miss.
procedure: Attempt 1: Codex CLI review. Attempt 2: independent general-purpose agent, read-only, allowed to build and run the tests.
expected_result: Ranked defect list; valid findings fixed and covered by tests.
observed_result: Codex could not run: its shell and file runtime failed at startup with CryptUnprotectData error 2148073483 (a Windows DPAPI/credential problem in the Codex sandbox), so it read no code. The independent reviewer found nothing critical and no memory-safety defects, and reported: (1) 16-bit player/entity ids could wrap to 0 under repeated joins, breaking snapshots for everyone; (2) the host input backlog never drained after jitter; (3) retransmitted ConnectRequests did not refresh liveness; (4) a slot in its grace period could be destroyed by a token-less request; (5) a stale ConnectAccept from an earlier attempt was accepted; (6) the prediction test passed without prediction; (7) the reconnect test comment was wrong about client b; (8) the heavy-loss test is only a smoke test; (9) low flakiness risk from fixed yield counts. Fixed: 1-7 (id exhaustion rejects with ServerFull; drain to a backlog of 2; liveness refresh; grace slots reclaimable by token only; nonce echoed in ConnectAccept and regenerated per reconnect; the prediction test now runs at 200 ms RTT and asserts authority has not moved yet; the reconnect test asserts b's reconnect). New test: id_exhaustion_rejects_instead_of_wrapping. Not fixed: 8 (accepted as a smoke test) and 9 (no flake observed in 13+ runs). No dedicated test covers the backlog drain.
follow_up: Re-run the Codex review after fixing its Windows credential issue. Add a backlog-drain test with jitter.
